info.description:
Manage the MCPs of a Quilr MCP Gateway tenant programmatically: inventory, creation and removal, settings, upstream credentials, tool reviews, OAuth connections and analytics.

**Authentication.** A tenant administrator enables management for the tenant and issues management keys in the Quilr console (MCP Gateway, Management API tab) or with the Administration endpoints (tenant administrator token). Every other endpoint takes a management key as `Authorization: Bearer qmcpmgmt_...`. Each operation lists the scopes it always requires in `x-scopes`; `x-conditional-scopes` lists scopes that are added when the request body carries credentials or settings. An empty `x-scopes` on an Administration operation means a tenant administrator token.

**Writes.** Changes to an existing MCP configuration require `If-Match` with the quoted `version` (ETag) from the latest read (`428` when missing, `412` when stale). Creates take an `Idempotency-Key`; retrying with the same key within 24 hours returns the original result instead of creating twice.

**Responses.** Every JSON response carries `request_id` (also in `X-Request-ID`) and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Errors use `{"error": {"code", "message", ...}, "request_id"}`; `error.fields` names the offending request paths and never echoes submitted values. Lists are paginated with `limit` and an opaque `cursor` (`next_cursor` is null on the last page). Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339 (`...Z`).

**Policy.** When QuilrQL policies govern the tenant, stored MCP settings are saved but not enforced until the policy engine is turned off; responses flag this with an `inactive_under_quilrql` warning.

post.description: A new single-use link (15 minutes) for an OAuth MCP whose sign-in the gateway manages. The link itself authorizes the connection: whoever opens it within 15 minutes, once, is sent to the provider's sign-in, and the connection they make is saved for the administrator who owns this management key (no console sign-in). Treat the URL as a short-lived credential and share it only with the person who should connect the account. The token is in the URL fragment; the landing page posts it to `POST /mcpgateway/management-connect/start` (`{"token": "..."}`, no authentication; answers `{mcp_id, mcp_name, authorization_url}`, or 404 `connect_link_not_found`, 409 `connect_link_used`, 410 `connect_link_expired` / `connect_link_revoked`, 409 `key_owner_unavailable`, 403 `management_disabled_for_tenant`, 429 `rate_limited`, 502 `oauth_initiation_failed`). 409 `oauth_not_applicable` for MCPs that do not use gateway-managed OAuth.
